root_cause.text: `bpf_prog_detach()` failed to enforce any privilege check for tcx/netkit multi-prog detaches when `attr->attach_bpf_fd` was not provided, allowing the empty-detach path to bypass the `CAP_NET_ADMIN`/`CAP_SYS_ADMIN` permission gate in the `BPF_PROG_DETACH` syscall handling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `bpf_mprog_detach_empty()` in `include/linux/bpf_mprog.h` that returns `bpf_net_capable()` for `BPF_PROG_TYPE_SCHED_CLS`, and `kernel/bpf/syscall.c` now rejects the no-`attach_bpf_fd` case with `return -EPERM;` unless that check passes; the commit message explicitly says detach on tcx/netkit could be executed by any user when no program fd was provided, bypassing permission checks.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: `bpf_prog_detach()` failed to enforce any privilege check for tcx/netkit multi-prog detaches when `attr->attach_bpf_fd` was not provided, allowing the empty-detach path to bypass the `CAP_NET_ADMIN`/`CAP_SYS_ADMIN` permission gate in the `BPF_PROG_DETACH` syscall handling.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `bpf_mprog_detach_empty()` in `include/linux/bpf_mprog.h` that returns `bpf_net_capable()` for `BPF_PROG_TYPE_SCHED_CLS`, and `kernel/bpf/syscall.c` now rejects the no-`attach_bpf_fd` case with `return -EPERM;` unless that check passes; the commit message explicitly says detach on tcx/netkit could be executed by any user when no program fd was provided, bypassing permission checks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to centralize network-related privilege checking for BPF code.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function `bpf_net_capable(void)` was added, returning `capable(CAP_NET_ADMIN) || capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN)`, and it was inserted before `bpf_probe_read_kernel_common()`.
intent_record.how: This provides a reusable capability check for code paths that need network-administration privileges, allowing either `CAP_NET_ADMIN` or the broader `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` to satisfy the check at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a capability-gated helper to determine when empty BPF multi-program detach is allowed for sched_cls programs.
intent_record.what: A new inline helper function, `bpf_mprog_detach_empty(enum bpf_prog_type type)`, was added. It switches on `type` and returns `bpf_net_capable()` only for `BPF_PROG_TYPE_SCHED_CLS`; for all other program types it returns `false`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a type-specific check for whether an empty detach operation is permitted, enabling the caller to allow detach behavior only for scheduler classifier BPF programs and only when the current context has network capability.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused `bpf_net_capable()` helper that wrapped CAP_NET_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability checks.
intent_record.what: The static helper function `bpf_net_capable()` was deleted. That function previously returned `capable(CAP_NET_ADMIN) || capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN)`.
intent_record.how: This removes a dedicated capability check wrapper from this source file, so any remaining callers must use another path or the check is no longer needed here. The runtime behavior of this specific code block changes only by eliminating that helper definition; it no longer provides a local way to test for network/admin privileges.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject unsupported BPF program detach requests by returning -EPERM when empty multi-program detach is not allowed.
intent_record.what: In bpf_prog_detach(), after the existing check that loads the program by FD when attach_bpf_fd is provided, a new else-if branch was added: if bpf_mprog_detach_empty(ptype) is false, the function now returns -EPERM before continuing.
intent_record.how: This prevents detach operations from proceeding for program types that do not support empty multi-program detach semantics unless the caller supplied a specific BPF program FD, causing unsupported detach requests to fail with a permission error instead of being accepted.

grouping_result.intent: Add a helper to centralize network-related privilege checking for BPF code.
Add a capability-gated helper to determine when empty BPF multi-program detach is allowed for sched_cls programs.
Remove the unused `bpf_net_capable()` helper that wrapped CAP_NET_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability checks.
Reject unsupported BPF program detach requests by returning -EPERM when empty multi-program detach is not allowed.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a centralized helper for network-related privilege checks in general, but the vulnerability is specifically about missing enforcement in the tcx/netkit empty-detach path of `bpf_prog_detach()`. The summary does not indicate a fix to that detach permission bypass.

The change adds a capability-gated helper for allowing empty BPF multi-program detach, which directly matches the root cause: missing privilege enforcement on the empty-detach path in bpf_prog_detach().

The change only removes an unused capability-check helper. It does not fix or modify the missing privilege check in `bpf_prog_detach()` for empty-detach tcx/netkit multi-prog detaches, which is the reported root cause.

The change directly targets the empty-detach path in BPF_PROG_DETACH by rejecting unsupported detach requests with -EPERM, which addresses the privilege-check bypass described in the root cause for tcx/netkit multi-prog detaches when no attach_bpf_fd is provided.

candidates.rationale: This is the start of the attach_bpf_fd-dependent branch; the vulnerability occurs in the complementary empty-detach path when attach_bpf_fd is absent, so this statement helps identify the code path that bypassed any privilege enforcement.

This shows the conditional structure handling different detach cases. The bug is in the empty-detach path for tcx/netkit multi-prog detaches, which was processed by a similar unchecked branch before the fix.

The root cause is the missing privilege check in the complementary empty-detach path, so this statement identifies the code path where the bypass occurred.

This conditional shows the alternative detach-path handling after the attach_bpf_fd-dependent branch. It is part of the pre-fix control flow that allowed the empty-detach case for tcx/netkit multi-prog detaches to proceed without enforcing CAP_NET_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

This validation only rejects certain detach inputs, but it does not enforce a privilege check for the empty-detach case when attach_bpf_fd is absent. That omission is the vulnerability described in the root cause.
